title: Fisher’s Hornpipe
short: Traditional (British, 1700s), long playe · G 4/4 · play it with every note lit.

blocks.html: A bright hornpipe that came over from the British Isles and stayed in the fiddle and banjo repertoire of the South. In this arrangement almost every eighth note is a note of the tune, picked T I M without using a finger twice in a row. In bars 9 to 12 the left hand moves up to the 7th fret, where a D chord lies across the top three strings; in bars 13 and 14 the fingers fall into C and G roll shapes.

blocks.name: music-player
blocks.cap: Play it: the score scrolls, the keys or strings light up as each note sounds.

blocks.html: The piece: Hornpipe, printed in many collections from the late 1700s on

sources.name: Melody checked note by note against “Fisher’s Hornpipe” in Ryan’s Mammoth Collection (Boston, 1883), as transcribed in ABC at MIT (trillian.mit.edu, contributed by John Chambers). Moved from F to G and down an octave; the fiddle’s sixteenth notes are our eighth notes, and the pickups are left out. Every note of that version is in our tab at its time, except where a bar ends with a held note. Chords are ours.
